questions.q: What is the real PostgreSQL object hierarchy, per this lesson?
options: Cluster, then database, then schema, then table
Database, then cluster, then table, then schema
Schema, then cluster, then database, then table
Table, then schema, then cluster, then database
questions.explain: A cluster manages one or more databases, each database contains schemas, and each schema contains tables and other objects.

questions.q: Why can't you write a simple three-part-name query joining tables in two different PostgreSQL databases the way you can in SQL Server, per this lesson?
options: PostgreSQL connections are scoped to exactly one database; cross-database queries require an extension like postgres_fdw or dblink
PostgreSQL does not support joins of any kind
PostgreSQL databases and schemas are the exact same object
SQL Server also cannot do cross-database queries, so the comparison doesn't apply
questions.explain: Unlike SQL Server's three-part naming across databases, PostgreSQL isolates databases at the connection level, requiring extensions for cross-database access.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the difference between how schemas are typically used in SQL Server versus PostgreSQL?
options: SQL Server treats schemas mainly as a permission/ownership grouping, while PostgreSQL practice leans on schemas more heavily as a genuine organizational namespace, such as one schema per tenant
SQL Server and PostgreSQL use schemas in an identical way with no practical difference
PostgreSQL does not support schemas at all
SQL Server schemas span multiple databases while PostgreSQL schemas cannot
questions.explain: The lesson draws an honest comparison: SQL Server schemas are mostly a permission layer, while PostgreSQL schemas are used more as real, first-class namespaces, including multi-tenancy patterns.

questions.q: What does a PostgreSQL tablespace control, per this lesson?
options: Where on disk a database or object's files physically live, independent of the logical database/schema/table hierarchy
Which users are permitted to query a given table
The order in which schemas are searched for unqualified table names
Whether a table participates in streaming replication
questions.explain: A tablespace is a physical storage location; it is separate from the logical hierarchy and is conceptually similar to SQL Server filegroups on different disks.

questions.q: What does the search_path setting control, per this lesson?
options: Which schemas are checked, and in what order, when a query references an unqualified table name
Which tablespace new databases are created in by default
The physical disk location of the WAL directory
Which roles are allowed to connect from a given IP address
questions.explain: search_path determines the order in which schemas are searched when a table name isn't explicitly qualified with a schema.
